description: YOUR BRIEF: release/SPEC.md exists and states what done means — requirements written before the gate was designed
command: S=release/SPEC.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'done means' $S && echo authored || echo incomplete

description: YOUR BRIEF: no CLAUDE.md under release/ — a build brief is an input to one task, not context injected into every future turn
command: [ -f release/CLAUDE.md ] && echo present || echo absent

description: YOUR GATE: release/ci-release-gate.sh exists and is executable — the release gate runs without you, which is the difference between a gate and a habit
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: EXIT PROTOCOL: the gate exits 2 on the known-bad candidate — block is its own code, not a generic failure
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; ./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: EXIT PROTOCOL: the gate exits 0 on a candidate that clears the analysers — it blocks on evidence, not on everything
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; C=$(ls release/tests/fixtures/*.yaml 2>/dev/null | head -1); [ -n "$C" ] || { echo no-good-fixture; exit 0; }; ./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values "$C" >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: FAIL-CLOSED: a candidate file it cannot read exits 1, NOT 0 and not 2 — the dangerous failure of a gate is approving a release it never examined
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; ./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values fixtures/release/does-not-exist.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: FAIL-CLOSED: run with no --values the gate refuses rather than silently analysing some default candidate
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; ./release/ci-release-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 1 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: FAIL-CLOSED: nothing is printed on stdout when the gate cannot evaluate — a verdict object on a fail-closed path is something downstream will misread
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; out=$(./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values fixtures/release/does-not-exist.yaml 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$out" ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: AUDITABILITY: the verdict names the candidate it judged — six weeks later this is what says it read the release and not the default
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; out=$(./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml 2>/dev/null); echo "$out" | jq -e '.candidate | test("candidate-values")' >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: AUDITABILITY: every blocker names where the finding came from — 'failed policy check' is a mood, not a finding
command: [ -x release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; out=$(./release/ci-release-gate.sh --values fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml 2>/dev/null); n=$(echo "$out" | jq '[.blockers[] | select(.source != null and .source != "")] | length' 2>/dev/null); t=$(echo "$out" | jq '.blockers | length' 2>/dev/null); { [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" = "$t" ] && [ "$t" -gt 0 ]; } && echo pass || echo fail

description: AUTHORITY: the gate contains no command that tags, pushes, deploys or applies — a gate that can ship is not a gate
command: [ -f release/ci-release-gate.sh ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; sed 's/#.*$//' release/ci-release-gate.sh | grep -Eq '(git[[:space:]]+tag|git[[:space:]]+push|docker[[:space:]]+push|helm[[:space:]]+(upgrade|install)|kubectl[[:space:]]+apply)' && echo ships || echo reports-only

description: SHELL TRAPS: the gate sets pipefail and captures an analyser's exit status explicitly, rather than trusting $? after a pipeline
command: G=release/ci-release-gate.sh; [ -f $G ] || { echo no-gate; exit 0; }; grep -q 'pipefail' $G && grep -Eq '[a-z_]+_rc=\$\?' $G && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR TESTS: a runner plus at least three executable test files live next to the gate
command: T=release/tests; [ -x $T/run.sh ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; n=$(ls $T/*.test.sh 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); x=$(find $T -name '*.test.sh' -perm -u+x 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); { [ "$n" -ge 3 ] && [ "$x" = "$n" ]; } && echo authored || echo missing

description: YOUR TESTS: the suite asserts on all three exit codes — approve, block AND cannot-evaluate. The third is the one nobody exercises by accident
command: T=release/tests; ls $T/*.test.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo missing; exit 0; }; for c in 0 1 2; do grep -hqE "eq[[:space:]]+$c|== *$c" $T/*.test.sh || { echo "missing-$c"; exit 0; }; done; echo complete

description: YOUR TESTS: the suite passes from a single command and exits 0
command: [ -x release/tests/run.sh ] || { echo no-suite; exit 0; }; ./release/tests/run.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: YOUR TESTS ACTUALLY WORK: turning the fail-closed path into a warning makes the suite fail — an assertion never seen failing proves nothing
command: G=release/ci-release-gate.sh; [ -x $G ] && [ -x release/tests/run.sh ] || { echo no-artifact; exit 0; }; cp $G /tmp/m13-gate-orig.sh; sed -i.bak 's/exit 1; }/exit 0; }/' $G 2>/dev/null; ./release/tests/run.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; cp /tmp/m13-gate-orig.sh $G; rm -f $G.bak; [ $rc -ne 0 ] && echo caught || echo blind

description: CI: the deterministic gate runs on pull requests from .github/workflows/release-gate.yml
command: W=.github/workflows/release-gate.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'pull_request' $W && grep -q 'ci-release-gate.sh' $W && echo shipped || echo incomplete

description: CI: the workflow branches on the gate's exit code so a block and a fail-closed do not report the same thing — they send you to different places
command: W=.github/workflows/release-gate.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q "rc == '2'" $W && grep -q "rc == '1'" $W && echo separated || echo collapsed

description: CI: the deterministic workflow references no secret and takes read-only repository permission — a gate that needs a credential is doing someone else's job
command: W=.github/workflows/release-gate.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; ! grep -q 'secrets\.' $W && grep -q 'contents: read' $W && echo clean || echo overprivileged

description: CI: the Claude workflow pins anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 and authenticates with an OAuth token, so a Pro/Max subscription works without an API key
command: W=.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'anthropics/claude-code-action@v1' $W && grep -q 'claude_code_oauth_token' $W && echo pass || echo fail

description: AUTHORITY: the model in CI gets an allow-list with no Edit or Write — it explains a verdict and cannot change the candidate, the gate or the tests
command: W=.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; a=$(grep -o '\-\-allowedTools[^\n]*' $W | head -1); [ -n "$a" ] || { echo unbounded; exit 0; }; echo "$a" | grep -Eq '(Edit|Write|MultiEdit)' && echo can-edit || echo read-only

description: COST: the CI model run is capped with --max-turns — an agent in a pipeline with no turn cap is an unbounded bill and an unbounded runtime
command: W=.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q -- '--max-turns' $W && echo bounded || echo unbounded

description: AUTHORITY: the review workflow cannot fail or pass the merge — it holds pull-requests: write to comment and nothing else; the gate and the typed verdict hold merge authority
command: W=.github/workflows/claude-pr-review.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'contents: read' $W && ! grep -q 'contents: write' $W && echo cannot-gate || echo can-gate

description: HOUSE STANDARD: the gate-style skill exists and carries the three-code protocol — handing TDD to the harness needs a standard it can read
command: S=.claude/skills/gate-style/SKILL.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'cannot evaluate' $S && grep -q 'fail-closed' $S && echo present || echo thin

description: HOUSE STANDARD: the skill names the shell constructs that silently turn a block into an approval — pipefail, $? after a pipe, grep under set -e
command: S=.claude/skills/gate-style/SKILL.md; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'pipefail' $S && grep -q 'set -e' $S && echo complete || echo thin

description: HARNESS: the release-engineer role carries the Skill tool — without it the agent reads SKILL.md as a plain file and no method runs
command: grep -E '^tools:' .claude/agents/release-engineer.md 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"Skill"' && echo capable || echo silently-degraded

description: AUTHORITY: the role that builds the gate is declared unable to tag, push or deploy, and unable to approve its own release
command: R=.claude/agents/release-engineer.md; [ -f $R ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qi 'NEVER.*git tag' $R && grep -qi 'never the approver' $R && echo bounded || echo unbounded

description: AUTHORITY: the role exists in contracts/authority-matrix.yaml with write authority over release/ — a role file alone is not a declared authority
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh release-engineer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] && echo capable || echo blocked

description: SEPARATION OF DUTIES: the change-reviewer has no write tool — the reviewer that edits the candidate has stopped being a reviewer
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh change-reviewer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo blocked || echo capable

description: HEADLESS SURFACE: claude -p --output-format json is the documented pipeline shape, and the lab's stage isolates MCP so its stdout stays parseable
command: grep -q 'output-format json' site/docs/m13-cicd-release/lab.md 2>/dev/null || grep -rq 'output-format json' . --include='*.md' 2>/dev/null; echo present

description: ANALYSER: pipeline-analyze.sh blocks the release candidate on its own — the gate composes this rule rather than re-implementing it
command: scripts/pipeline-analyze.sh --values fixtures/release/candidate-values.yaml --field verdict 2>/dev/null

description: ANALYSER: canary-verify.sh is executable — the second evidence source the gate composes when a canary snapshot is supplied
command: [ -x scripts/canary-verify.sh ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: CHANGE GATE: a production terraform apply is still denied from an agent identity (exit 2) — release tooling does not widen that
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform -chdir=infra/environments/prod apply"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: CHANGE GATE: docker push is denied from an agent identity (exit 2) — images ship from CI, and the gate never ships at all
command: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"docker push orders-api:latest"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: TYPED VERDICT: release/verdict.schema.json exists and constrains verdict to ship/hold/block — a pipeline branches on a field, not on prose
command: S=release/verdict.schema.json; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; jq -e '.properties.verdict.enum == ["ship","hold","block"]' $S >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo typed || echo untyped

description: TYPED VERDICT: rollback is a required field — a release decision that cannot say how to undo itself is rejected by the schema, not by a reviewer's attention
command: S=release/verdict.schema.json; [ -f $S ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; jq -e '.required | index("rollback") != null' $S >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo required || echo optional

description: AUTHORITY: the release-decider role has no file-write tool and is denied Edit/Write — it decides from the gate's output and cannot change what it judges
command: R=.claude/agents/release-decider.md; [ -f $R ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -qE '^disallowedTools:.*"Write"' $R && ! grep -qE '^tools:.*"Write"' $R && echo bounded || echo unbounded

description: HARNESS: the release-decider role carries Skill — without it the role reads a procedure as a plain file and improvises
command: grep -E '^tools:' .claude/agents/release-decider.md 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"Skill"' && echo capable || echo silently-degraded

description: CI: the verdict workflow emits schema-validated structured_output and pins the run without --bare — bare mode cannot read a subscription token, so using it would force an API key
command: W=.github/workflows/release-verdict.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q -- '--json-schema' $W && grep -q 'structured_output' $W && grep -q -- '--strict-mcp-config' $W && echo typed || echo untyped

description: CI: a job fails the build when system/init reports plugin_errors or mcp_server_errors — a skill or role that silently did not load becomes a red build
command: W=.github/workflows/agent-load-check.yml; [ -f $W ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'plugin_errors' $W && grep -q 'mcp_server_errors' $W && echo present || echo incomplete

description: AUTHORITY: no workflow hands Claude a deploy command — deploy authority belongs to a pipeline step, never to the model
command: ls .github/workflows/*.yml >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -lE 'kubectl (apply|delete)|helm (upgrade|install)|docker push|git tag' .github/workflows/*.yml >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo can-deploy || echo cannot-deploy

description: NO API KEY: no workflow requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — every Claude invocation in this project authenticates with a subscription OAuth token from `claude setup-token`
command: ls .github/workflows/*.yml >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -lq 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' .github/workflows/*.yml 2>/dev/null && echo needs-api-key || echo subscription-only
